newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends down on USDA output estimate.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends down on USDA output estimate.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled broadly lower on spillover pressure from other U.S. wheat markets after USDA forecast the largest U.S. wheat crop in three years, traders said.

U.S. wheat markets struggled after USDA released wheat production figures that came in higher than analysts' estimates, traders said. In the June crop report, USDA estimated 1997-98 U.S. HRW wheat production at 921 million bushels, above analysts' average expectation of 899 million.
Fund-related selling and technical sell stops also compounded the drop in wheat prices Thursday.
"There was not a lot of individual feature in our market -- we were basically lower in sympathy with (Kansas City and Chicago wheat futures)," a MGE trader said.
But MGE traders said ongoing dry conditions in western North Dakota and scale-down buying helped limit the kind of losses seen in KCBT and CBOT nearby wheat futures.
MGE spring wheat settled 8-1/4 to 11 cents per bushel lower, with July down 8-1/4 cents at $4.01-1/2 a bushel. New crop September lost 9-3/4 cents at $3.93-1/4.
Atwood-Peavey was a featured player, selling one million July and 2.5 million Sept bushels.
